chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from his brother Ali ibn Sayf, from his father Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from a man from the Banu Nawfal ibn al-Mutalib, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
The companions most loved by God, the Exalted, are four. And if a group exceeds seven, their noise and chatter only increase.
ai.seo_question: Who are the four companions most loved by God according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal highlights the spiritual excellence of the four most beloved companions to God, a group often identified in Shia tradition as Ali, Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman, or specifically Ali and the Ahl al-Bayt depending on the interpretive context. The mention of 'seven' serves as a threshold for the onset of 'laghath' (confusion or excessive noise), suggesting that while small, focused groups maintain spiritual clarity, larger assemblies risk losing coherence and divine presence.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-82 Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Sayf, on the authority of his brother Ali ibn Sayf, on the authority of his father Sayf ibn Umayrih, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Musa, on the authority of someone from the progeny of Nofl ibn al-Mutalib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said,
“The companions (on a trip) most loved by the Honorable the Exalted God are four. They will talk a lot and make too much noise if they are more than seven.”
